text:
Maya: Quick thought  we should show a lightweight console transient when auto-fallback happens that explains: why, how confident we are, and what were sampling for QA. Want to iron out the UX and telemetry.
Rohan: Agree. Terms: banner vs toast vs snackbar? I prefer a non-modal toast with an attachable history item.
Jules: Call it a 'toast' if it's dismissible but pinnable to the top of the Fallback Timeline.
Ana: What about a numeric confidence field? "confidence score" 0-100. Helps prioritize alerts.
Maya: Exactly. Confidence = function(error_rate_1m, latency_ratio, recent_success_rate, model-mismatch). We'll start simple.
Rohan: Need to avoid confusion with existing "reason_code". So show both: REASON (code) + CONFIDENCE (score) + brief human sentence.
Jules: Add a small action set: [Investigate] [Revert] [Mark false positive]. Revert should queue a re-eval attempt, not instant swap.
Ana: If operator chooses "Mark false positive" we should capture that decision and attach the sampled traces to the event, and bump a tag for SRE review.
telemetry-bot: note: we'd like a stable id on events for correlation -> propose header X-Fallback-Event = <uuid>.
Maya: Good. Also we should sample a small percentage of live requests and store anonymized inputs for evaluation. Default sample rate 1% during probation.
Rohan: UX: toast text like: "Auto-fallback to quant-small (reason: p95-latency spike) — confidence 78% — probation 4m — [Open event]". Clicking open lands you in the Fallback Timeline filtered to that id.
Jules: For privacy, sampled inputs should be redacted unless org opts-in. Store fingerprints (sha256) and scalar metrics for search.
Ana: On the API side, emit an event to our ingestion pipeline `fallback.triggered` with minimal fields: fallback_event_id, timestamp, reason_code, confidence, probation_seconds, primary_model, fallback_model, sample_link(s).
Maya: Also surface fallback_event_id in request-level logs so SREs can jump from logs -> replay.
Rohan: One more: probation semantics. During probation, we route X% of traffic back to primary model to check drift. If mismatch < threshold, we auto-recover. Configurable per-org.
Jules: Suggest a default probation of 5 minutes and 0.5% traffic back to primary for production, 2% for staging.
Ana: Need an operator flow for "undo fallback" which triggers immediate traffic split rollback and forces a deeper evaluation run. That action should create an audit entry and be rate-limited.
telemetry-bot: recorded feature-flag: fallback_toast_rollout = 10% for staging.
Carla: Risk: too many toasts will annoy product teams. We should gate visible to users by confidence threshold (e.g., show only if confidence >= 65) and add a verbosity toggle on the Team settings.
Maya: Agreed. Default to conservative (higher precision). Provide a "verbose console" toggle for early adopters.
Rohan: Action items: Maya write UX spec + text strings, Jules wire Fallback Timeline link behavior, Ana implement header + sampling + redact opt-in, Carla draft Playbook for SRE + Support.
Jules: I'll mock the toast and the pinned timeline item tomorrow.
Maya: Can we schedule 15m tomorrow to review mocks? I'll send invite and include SRE + Support.
Carla: I'll prepare example Playbook steps for confidence buckets: 90+, 70-90, <70.
Maya: Cool. Thanks all. :rocket:
